subject: Career
title: Giving Feedback That Lands
description: A quick win: understand Giving Feedback That Lands.

hook.text: He said: 'Your work needs improvement.' She heard: 'You're a failure.' Vague feedback creates defensiveness.

buildup.text: Effective feedback is specific, timely, and behavior-focused — not character-focused.

discovery.text: The SBI model works: Situation (when), Behavior (what), Impact (the effect). No judgments, just observations.

twist.text: Most people wait too long to give feedback. By then, resentment has built and the moment is lost.

climax.text: Give feedback within 24 hours. Be specific. Focus on one behavior at a time. Ask for their perspective.

punchline.text: Feedback isn't criticism. It's a gift — when delivered with precision and care.

quiz.question: What does the SBI feedback model stand for?

details.summary: Feedback that lands is feedback the recipient can hear, internalize, and act on. This requires reading the emotional state of the recipient, choosing the right moment, and framing observations in a way that feels supportive rather than threatening to their identity.
details.whyItMatters: Even perfectly accurate feedback fails if the recipient becomes defensive. Learning to deliver feedback that is received, rather than just delivered, is what separates good managers from great ones.
takeaways: Time your feedback for when the recipient is ready to hear it
Ask permission before giving feedback to lower defensiveness
Frame corrections as observations, not character judgments

faq.question: How do I know if someone is emotionally ready to receive feedback?
faq.answer: Look for indicators of stress like distraction, visible frustration, or a just-finished crisis. Ask a simple check-in like 'Is now a good time for some feedback on the project?' This signals respect and gives them the option to defer if needed.

faq.question: What is the difference between feedback that is given and feedback that lands?
faq.answer: Given feedback is information transmitted. Feedback that lands is information received, understood, and acted upon. The gap between the two is closed by empathy, timing, relationship trust, and framing the message around shared goals rather than personal shortcomings.
